targetAudience.primary: Agent-runtime, digital-employee and AI governance engineers who design human approval boundaries for consequential tool calls
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands user-role messages, tool confirmations and basic authorization concepts.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A response can be syntactically valid user input yet originate from a remote agent that is not authorized to satisfy a human approval gate.

whyNow: A same-day merged Google ADK change demonstrates a receiver-owned A2A origin marker and an early fail-closed confirmation check, including the no-peer-metadata case that previously allowed origin to disappear.

externalHook.description: Message role describes content semantics; it does not by itself establish which trust domain produced the approval.

coreProposition: Agent runtimes should qualify receiver-controlled origin provenance before treating user-role content as accountable human approval; positive human authentication and authorization remain separate gates.

originalValue.description: Separates content role, transport origin, principal identity, authorization scope and approval occurrence identity into distinct approval evidence rather than overloading role=user.

readerTakeaway: Fail closed on disallowed origin classes before approval matching, then authenticate and authorize the positive approver independently and bind that decision to the exact approval occurrence.

supported: Merged ADK code always marks A2A-originated invocations with receiver-owned a2a_metadata, even when peer metadata is empty or absent.
The changed confirmation processor returns before confirmation-event resolution when the A2A marker is present.
Regression tests cover metadata-present and no-metadata A2A requests.
unsupported: Authentication of the eventual human approver
Coverage of every transport and confirmation processor
uncertain: How mixed-origin workflows should transition to a legitimate later human approval
How delegated non-human approvers should be represented without being mistaken for humans

firstPartyRole.rationale: The judgment concerns a general trust boundary for agent approvals and does not depend on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The same-day merged implementation provides a concrete negative origin gate, and the Research Object contributes an independently useful, explicitly bounded approval-evidence model.
